title: Part II
text: Part II AESTHETIC THEORY Contrive a poem out of ears. Tell it so that its petals unchocolate like a brain in ajar. Wax walnut, melting with thought. Make it a poem almost lewdly knowledgable and make its knowledge ooze, syrup from the punched trunk. Make it snake up to the molecule whorey and put its mouth atomic against the mouth of its core. Pull on its stem to expose its foetus. Make it have children with sleek ginger jaws, make the dogs moan when it passes, let it out of its jar, make it lie with our corpse, our chaos. Make it hungry, evil, enemy of Death. Put it on paper. Read it. Make surgery its sigh, and of such sting the scorpions call it Jehovah & Who. Make it now before you crap out. Contrive it, sperm it, stroke it, make it efficient, make it fit, make it more poem than Poem can survive. Stan Rice, Some Lamb 1975
